subject: Production QoS window misbind — customer-facing suppression, immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: Aaron Meyers <aaron@brightline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+platform@brightline.com
Date: 2025-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden suppression of throughput around 08:50 PDT — impacting nightly billing window

Karthik —

We started seeing a large drop in successful inference throughput at ~08:50 PDT this morning. Latency spiked from ~180ms to 900-1200ms and a subset of requests started returning 429/503. This is hitting our nightly billing/aggregation window and causing downstream jobs to timeout.

Quick data:
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: rdx-large)
- Error pattern: 5xx + 429s clustered between 08:50–09:05
- Traffic shape: short spikes ~2–3k qps for 20s, then normalizing

Can you confirm whether this is an intentional safety valve or a policy misconfiguration on your side? We need a short-term fix (disable whatever's suppressing us?) and a mitigation so our SLAs don't get dinged.

Aaron
Director, Platform Engineering
Brightline Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Meyers <aaron@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden suppression of throughput around 08:50 PDT — impacting nightly billing window

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the data. We're investigating now.

Quick note on next steps (internal and shared):
- Monica / Vanessa: can you run an immediate audit of the per-account QoS mapping and active safety valves for Brightline (DL-8372)? Prioritize active window rules and any recent policy pushes between 08:00–09:30.
- I'll request an emergency capacity bump for the dedicated pool and consider disabling the account-level safety valve if we confirm a misbind.

Aaron — I will update in 15–20m with an initial mitigation. Apologies for the disruption.

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T09:33:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden suppression of throughput — running policy snapshot now

Karthik / Vanessa — pulling policy snapshots. Attached: policy-snapshot-20251011.json (trimmed) and the throughput graphs. Early finding: a QoS window (named q-window:short_burst_safety) was linked to a route namespace that Brightline uses via an older mapping key (account_alias: brightline-v1). That alias was supposed to be deprecated in August; a recent policy consolidation PR (2025-10-10 23:14 UTC) merged alias routes but did not update the alias->account mapping for that safety valve.

This would cause Brightline traffic to match the safety valve inadvertently leading to suppression when short spikes occur. I'm going to simulate a remove of the alias and re-evaluate.

Monica
Director, Reliability Engineering
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Meyers <aaron@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden suppression of throughput around 08:50 PDT — immediate mitigation applied

Aaron — update: Monica found that an alias mapping caused Brightline to match a short-burst safety valve (q-window:short_burst_safety). We've temporarily disabled that safety valve for DL-8372 and applied an immediate capacity bump to the account's dedicated pool. Early telemetry shows errors and latency returning to baseline.

Short-term asks for Brightline:
- Please confirm if you still see elevated errors or timeouts in the next 15m and share any failing request ids.
- We'll keep the safety valve disabled until we complete the policy remap and run a smoke test.

Longer-term items we committed to (internal):
1) Audit and remove deprecated alias mappings and add a validation step to policy merges.
2) Add an automated overlap check that flags account->alias->safety-valve collisions.
3) Create a rollback playbook for safety-valve disables that records who toggled and why.

We will follow up with a post-mortem and corrective timeline by EOD. Apologies again — we'll treat this as high priority.

Karthik
From: Aaron Meyers <aaron@brightline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+platform@brightline.com
Date: 2025-10-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden suppression of throughput — thanks, seeing improvement

Karthik / team — thanks for the fast response. We're seeing success rates climb back to normal and downstream jobs are completing. I will send any failing request ids if I see residuals, but at this point the impact looks contained to the 08:50–09:05 window.

Two asks from our side:
- Can we get a written confirmation once you finish the alias cleanup + prevention checklist? We need this for our internal incident log.
- If possible, we'd like an assurance that safety valves will not be applied to our billing/aggregation routes without explicit opt-in.

Aaron
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident notes & next steps (INF-5421)

Summary: root cause = alias misbind created by a policy consolidation PR that didn't update alias->account mappings. Result was unintended matching of account traffic to q-window:short_burst_safety which suppresses short spikes and returns errors/429s under burst patterns. Brightline saw a 20–35% increase in latencies and clustered 429/503s for ~15m.

Actions completed:
- Safety valve disabled for DL-8372 at 09:40 PDT (temporary fix).
- Dedicated pool capacity bumped + traffic backfilled.
- Policy snapshot and affected PR identified (PR#2147, merged 2025-10-10).

Action plan (owners & target dates):
- Monica: purge deprecated alias mappings + push validation (2025-10-13).
- Vanessa: add an automated overlap detector to CI that blocks merges that create account-safety valve collisions (2025-10-20).
- Marcus: add a canary rollout for policy merges with a 24h monitoring window (2025-10-27).
- Karthik: own customer-facing communication and post-mortem delivery to Brightline (deliverable 2025-10-11 EOD).

Compliance note: Monica — please include the artifact (policy-snapshot-20251011.json) and telemetry graphs for their incident log.

Grace
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
